title: PostgreSQL BYTEA block store backend
description:
Implement PgBlockStore storing article blocks as BYTEA rows in a PostgreSQL table, using the same database connection as the metadata plane. Zero additional infrastructure for operators already running Aurora/PostgreSQL.

Why this issue exists:
Operators deploying on Aurora Serverless v2 for metadata already have a PostgreSQL connection. Adding a blocks table to the same database gives them a complete single-infrastructure deployment — no S3 bucket, no filesystem mount, no separate daemon. For small to medium single-operator instances this is entirely reasonable. The SQLite BLOB backend established the pattern; this is the PostgreSQL equivalent.

## Schema

CREATE TABLE blocks (
    cid       TEXT    NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    codec     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    data      BYTEA   NOT NULL,
    byte_size INTEGER NOT NULL,
    stored_at BIGINT  NOT NULL  -- unix ms
);

## What needs doing

- Add [backend.pg_blob] config section: database_url (reuses the same Aurora/PostgreSQL URL as the metadata plane; operator may configure a separate URL if preferred)
- Implement PgStore: IpfsStore (transit) and PgBlockStore: IpfsBlockStore (reader) using sqlx with the postgres driver
  - put: INSERT INTO blocks ... ON CONFLICT (cid) DO NOTHING — idempotent, CID is the natural unique key
  - get: SELECT data FROM blocks WHERE cid = ? — returns the BYTEA column; map no-row to None / NotFound
  - delete: DELETE FROM blocks WHERE cid = ? returning DeletionOutcome::Immediate
- IPNS: disable
- Startup: verify the blocks table exists (run migration); verify the connection is writable; fail fast if not
- WAL / connection pool: reuse the existing sqlx PgPool from the metadata plane if the database_url matches; do not open a second connection pool to the same database
- Migration: single migration file adding the blocks table, part of the PostgreSQL migration set from stoa-b38f9c00

## Transactional consistency bonus

Because both the metadata write (article_numbers, msgid_map) and the block write (blocks table) are in the same PostgreSQL instance, they can be wrapped in a single transaction:
- If the block write fails, the metadata entry is not committed
- If the metadata write fails, the block is not committed
- No orphaned CIDs in the block store with no metadata entry, and no metadata entries pointing to missing blocks
Document this as a design advantage in the runbook; it is unique to this backend pairing.

## Size guidance (in runbook)

- Suitable for: single-operator instances, small groups, up to ~50-100 GB of article bytes
- Not suitable for: high-volume feeds, binary groups (out of scope anyway), multi-operator shared infrastructure
- Aurora Serverless v2 autoscales storage automatically; operators do not need to pre-provision
- For larger deployments: migrate to S3 backend (export blocks table, upload to S3, switch config)

## GC / delete semantics

DeletionOutcome::Immediate. PostgreSQL DELETE is transactional and synchronous. The article is inaccessible as soon as the transaction commits. No grace period.

## Acceptance criteria
- Round-trip test: put a block, get it back, assert bytes match (against a local PostgreSQL instance in CI via docker-compose)
- Idempotent put: inserting the same CID twice does not error and does not duplicate the row
- Transactional test: simulate a metadata write failure mid-transaction and confirm the block row was not committed
- delete() removes the row; get() returns NotFound immediately after
- delete() on a CID that does not exist returns Ok(DeletionOutcome::Immediate) without error
- Reuses the existing PgPool when database_url matches the metadata plane URL
